messages.author: a1a5bf01db5f48ce
messages.subject: not able to produce full HTML document
parts:
Hello,

I am having problems producing a HTML. I have used knitr before with no problems. 

Here is a sample of code:

-----------
#'----------------------------------------------------------------
#'Sara Blackburn     
#'January 13th, 2014
#' 
#'Programming in R     
#'Practical 1:2: Shortening our code using a function 
#----------------------------------------------------------------

#'Let's specify the important arguments and store them in a function called 'step.simple.growth'.
#'We can then call up the function in our loop. 

#Specify the updated population from the current count (P) and the additions (P(t+1)) 
#The function will return the last value called, in this case, updated.population

step.simple.growth <- function(current.count, this.growth.rate)
{
  new.additions <- this.growth.rate*current.count
  updated.population  <- current.count+new.additions
  updated.population
}
-----------

...obviously that's not complete but from that I would expect a HTML file with a title and all #' comments to appear clear, and all # comments to appear in the normal grey format.

However, I am only getting:

-----------
Sara Blackburn January 13th, 2014 Programming in R Practical 1:2: Shortening our code using a function
title: “0102-growth-functional.r” author: “Sara” date: “Wed Sep 24 10:58:46 2014”
-----------

...and that's it. 

I have updated all the packages, tried loading knitr manually, tried uninstalling, resetting, etc. Nothing is working.

Any advice as to what I am doing wrong?

I've attached the two files: the R code and the HTML that is being produced. 

Thanks
Sara

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] not able to produce full HTML document
parts:
RStudio has switched from R Markdown v1 to v2, which uses Pandoc to
process your Markdown output. Because --- means the YAML metadata for
Pandoc, basically your whole R script was treated as a YAML metadata
block. To learn more about how to use R notebooks in R Markdown v2,
see http://rmarkdown.rstudio.com/r_notebook_format.html You need to
change your metadata block to something like this:

#' ---
#' author: Sara Blackburn
#' date: January 13th, 2014
#' title: "Programming in R
#' Practical 1:2: Shortening our code using a function"

#' output: html_document
#' ---


Regards,
Yihui
--
Yihui Xie <xiey...@gmail.com>
Web: http://yihui.name

messages.subject: Re: not able to produce full HTML document
parts:
Hello Sarah,

In addition of Yihui's post, if you use the newest version of R Studio (Version 0.98.1049), you can go to:

Menu > New File > R Markdown

Then a window will pop up. Fill in the title of your file, the author, and the output type you wish to get (HTML in this case). Then R Studio will make a YAML header (like the one Yihui showed).

Then you can copy paste the code from your R code file, add some stories about it. Then if you finish, just click the "knit HTML" button on the menu bar.

I hope that helps.

Erwin

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Re: not able to produce full HTML document
parts:
Please follow my last reply carefully: first, you probably should not
remove the spaces after #', although I do not think this is the
problem; second, if your title spans across two lines, please indent
the second line by at least spaces.

Personally I find it much easier to use R Markdown documents directly,
instead of R notebooks, especially when you teach beginners, because
RStudio has extensive GUI support to R Markdown documents, e.g. you
can change the YAML metadata via the gear button on the toolbar (see
http://blog.rstudio.org/2014/06/18/r-markdown-v2/). Unless your
students are very familiar with the YAML syntax and R Markdown, I do
not R notebooks are an appropriate starting point (apparently it even
confuses you).

Regards,
Yihui
--
Yihui Xie <xiey...@gmail.com>
Web: http://yihui.name
